milestone: M30 Controlled Test Failure Diagnostics And Recovery Evidence

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Failed controlled cargo-test gates now carry bounded diagnostic handles that let headless recovery choose a next read or repair direction without raw process output.
Extends the existing Rust-owned verification.cargo_test tool result instead of adding generic process execution or caller-selected test execution.
Stores only sanitized bounded cargo-test diagnostic entries in existing ToolExecutionFailed and verification gate payloads.
Keeps ExecuteProcess gating, fixed cargo-test command selection, and runtime-owned parsing/redaction as the authority boundary.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting controlled_workspace_tools, persistent_structured_ledger, and runtime_permission_enforcement.
answers.new_capability: Failed launched verification.cargo_test runs can now emit at most five bounded diagnostics with hashed test identity and optional sanitized panic location through existing tool, ledger, gate, recovery provenance, and protocol paths.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M29.1 could execute the fixed cargo-test verifier but failures only provided status, bytes, truncation, and safety metadata. R3.3 cargo-check diagnostics do not describe test-harness failures.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Brownie can run tests but headless recovery still cannot tell which failed test or safe location to inspect without an external raw-output reader.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. The previous three phases added cargo-test execution, recovery apply continuation, and recovery routing; this phase changes the bounded evidence produced by failed cargo-test execution.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase reuses tool.execute, task.run, task.start recovery provenance, run.events, and existing protocol validation.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. It extends bounded verifier metadata and diagnostics arrays rather than adding a report, digest, history, readiness, preview, capability, or inspection surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Failed launched verification.cargo_test runs now produce sanitized cargo-test diagnostics that survive runtime ledger insertion and completion-gate propagation.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless recovery task can use deterministic test-name hashes and optional safe panic locations to select the next investigation step without raw stdout or stderr.
answers.milestone_progress: Starts M30 by making controlled test failures recoverable evidence instead of opaque verifier failures.

review_value_gate.review_intent: M30.1 must be reviewed for actual failed cargo-test diagnostic behavior, bounded redaction, runtime sanitizer propagation, no raw test output leakage, and no wrapper or new RPC surfaces.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M30.1 changes product/runtime evidence behavior and current phase manifests; guard engine changes are not expected.

exit_criteria: Failed launched verification.cargo_test runs emit at most five bounded diagnostics without raw stdout, stderr, rendered panic text, assertion values, source snippets, raw test names, commands, environment values, absolute paths, canonical paths, or file content.
Cargo-test diagnostics use deterministic SHA-256 test_name_hash values and optional sanitized workspace-relative panic locations.
Runtime sanitizer admits valid cargo-test diagnostic entries and rejects unsafe shapes before ledger or recovery propagation.
Failed task-scoped verification.cargo_test completion gates include bounded diagnostics in existing gate metadata.
VSIX protocol validation accepts valid cargo-test diagnostics and rejects raw test_name, invalid hashes, invalid paths, forbidden raw fields, unknown fields, and arrays over five.
No new RPC, report, digest, history, readiness, preview, capability, or inspection wrapper is added.

tests: runtime client bounded cargo diagnostic validation

next_phase_candidate_notes: After M30.1 lands, assess whether verification recovery retry can use cargo-test diagnostic handles to choose narrower reads while preserving the no-raw-output boundary. Do not add diagnostics report/history/inspection wrappers.
